title: C# Questions & Answers - Use of Variable Number of Arguments
sourceFile: C# Questions & Answers – Use of Variable Number of Arguments - Sanfoundry.html
description: This set of C# Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on "Use of Variable Number of Arguments".

questions.question: A method that can accept a variable number of arguments uses which kind of parameter?
questions.explanation: In C#, using the 'params' keyword allows you to pass a variable number of arguments to a method, which is internally handled as a parameter array.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: Passing an object[] to a params object[] parameter uses that array as the argument list. The loop prints every element. 4 is an int, so it is written as 4, not 4.0. The matching choice is 1 4 harsh.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about methods in C#?

options.text: C# does not allow functions to have default values
C# allows a function to have a variable number of arguments using 'params'
The params keyword can appear at any position in the parameter list
Omitting the return type causes a runtime exception

questions.explanation: params lets a method take a variable number of arguments, but that parameter must be the last one. C# does allow optional parameters with default values. A missing return type is a compile-time error, not a runtime exception.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: P R A H S C
C S H A R P

questions.explanation: Those integers are ASCII/Unicode codes: 80=P, 82=R, 65=A, 72=H, 83=S, 67=C. The loop prints from index 5 down to 0, so the characters are C S H A R P.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: A B C D E F
F E D C B A

questions.explanation: Adding 32 to an uppercase ASCII value converts it to lowercase (e.g., 70+32=102 which is 'f'). The loop runs from index 5 down to 1 (i > 0), so it prints f, e, d, c, b.
